text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- A lev/dollar exchange rate of 1,600 was assumed in the 1997 draft budget prepared by the interim cabinet and any rumours of a lev slump were not justified, Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said. @
-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to introduce a four percent retail surcharge for natural gas distributors in the country. The surcharge will replace the pegging of the gas price to the fuel oil price.
-- Bulgarian National Bank foreign exchange reserves totalled $1.25 billion at mid-May, up from $1.09 billion on April 21, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.

-- Bulgaria may face a pork shortage in the summer as local meat producers can not meet market demand and an import duty of $800 per tonne prevents imports, Association of the Bulgarian Meat Processors said.

-- Bulgaria hopes to complete restoration of ownership on arable land by the end-1998, the Agriculture ministry said. Some 54 percent of arable land has been returned to its original pre-communist owners.

-- Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces prime minister designate Ivan Kostov presented his cabinet to President Petar Stoyanov. The parliament is expected to vote the new government in office on Wednesday.
-- Bulgaria may cut electricity and coal prices by five to six percent from June 1 because April monthly inflation was below zero and lev has stabilised, Energy minister Georgi Stoilov said.

-- Bulgaria's Financial Stabilisation Council advising the interim government proposed to parliament to peg the lev to the German mark as anchor currency in a fixed exchange rate regime aimed to restore the confidence in the financial system, interim Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
